verdict: More customers trading more: accounts rose 35% to 5.58 million and net interest income jumped 19%, so the automated broker raised its dividend by 71%.

segments.name: Interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on customer margin loans and segregated cash — shown gross here; the interest paid out to customers is the chart's direct cost.

segments.name: Commissions
segments.note: Commissions on customer trades: daily average revenue trades rose 18% to 4.27 million, led by futures volume (+13%).

segments.name: Other fees & services
segments.note: Risk exposure fees, market data and payments for order flow from exchange programs.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Investing results and the currency diversification strategy (a $40M gain this quarter).

opex.name: Execution, clearing & distribution fees
opex.note: Fees paid to exchanges and clearing houses to execute and clear customer trades — up 46%, driven by a higher SEC transaction fee rate passed through to customers.

opex.name: Employee compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the (deliberately lean) staff of an automated broker.

opex.name: Occupancy, depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Offices, data centers and equipment wear-and-tear.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: General and administrative costs of $78M, less a $1M customer bad-debt credit.

follow100Note: This chart starts from gross revenue: $2,433M of interest income plus $760M of non-interest income. Paying $1,279M of interest to customers leaves the $1,914M of net revenue Interactive Brokers headlines (up 16%). Of the $1,348M bottom line, $1,034M belongs to non-controlling interests (the founding group's IBG LLC stake); $314M was available to common stockholders.

takeaways.title: A 78% pre-tax margin
takeaways.text: Automation keeps costs tiny relative to revenue: $418M of non-interest expenses against $1,914M of net revenue left $1,496M of pre-tax profit.

takeaways.title: Interest is the biggest earner
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 19% to $1,154M as customer margin loans grew 36% to $105B and customer credit balances reached $186B.

takeaways.title: Customer money keeps arriving
takeaways.text: Customer equity rose 27% to $965B and accounts grew 35% to 5.58 million — the base that future commissions and interest income are earned on.

oneTimers: Company-adjusted figures strip out $42M of net revenue (mainly currency-diversification and investment marks): adjusted net revenue was $1,872M and adjusted EPS $0.67, vs $0.69 GAAP.
